issue: The 2026 Blueprint renamed the Area II topic this lesson serves to 'Control environment, IT general controls, and entity-level controls' and revised two tasks to emphasize entity-level controls, but the lesson never uses or teaches the term 'entity-level control' (no other AUD lesson does either). aud-ic-13 tests it with no supporting teaching.
evidence: grep -i 'entity-level' over content/aud/modules/*/lesson.md returns 0 hits; the only content hit is aud-ic-13 in questions.json. review/reference/blueprint-notes.md, '2026 changes for AUD' item 2: topic renamed and 'two tasks in it were revised to emphasize entity-level controls'.
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint, Area II group C topic 1 (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md); PCAOB AS 2201.22-.27 (entity-level controls, top-down approach); COSO 2013
fix: Add a short section 'Entity-level vs. process-level controls': define ELCs (control environment, risk assessment, monitoring, period-end financial reporting process, management review controls, ITGCs as pervasive controls), distinguish indirect ELCs from precise ELCs that can address assertions (AS 2201.23-.24), explain why a weak control environment undermines process-level controls, and link ITGCs to aud-it-controls. Add a key takeaway, an inline check and 2 practice MCQs (one application, one analysis).

issue: The lesson never teaches the core AU-C 315 (SAS 145) requirements for understanding internal control: evaluate each component, determine whether control deficiencies exist, and evaluate the design and determine the implementation of specified controls (controls over significant risks, journal-entry controls, controls planned to be tested for operating effectiveness, others). No AUD lesson covers this; aud-tests-of-controls has one line on design vs operating effectiveness.
evidence: grep for 'implementation', 'design and implement', 'identified controls' across content/aud/modules/*/lesson.md finds nothing relevant; aud-tests-of-controls/lesson.md:64 has a single sentence. Yet aud-ic-06's explanation relies on 'evaluating design and implementation'. SAS 145 effective for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2023 (review/reference/aud-standards.md §2, verified) and is therefore tested in 2026.
source: AU-C 315 as amended by SAS 145 (understanding the components of the system of internal control; evaluating design and determining implementation of controls in the control activities component; identifying control deficiencies)
fix: Add a section 'What the auditor must do with internal control (AU-C 315)': understanding of each component; which controls require a D&I evaluation; D&I = inquiry plus observation/inspection/walkthrough (inquiry alone is not enough); D&I is not a test of operating effectiveness; if controls are not tested, control risk is assessed at maximum; deficiencies identified from the component evaluation feed AU-C 265. Add one inline check and one MCQ.

source: Review brief §3 (lesson-item alignment, sequencing)

issue: The 60-day AU-C 265 deadline is taught (lesson takeaway, aud-ic-03, flashcard f5) without the issuer contrast, although the lesson also teaches integrated audits under AS 2201. Under PCAOB standards the written communication of significant deficiencies and material weaknesses is due before the auditor's report is issued, and AS 2201 also requires communicating all deficiencies to management in writing. The takeaway, aud-ic-03's stem and f5's front carry no nonissuer qualifier.
evidence: Lesson takeaway: 'must be communicated in writing ... no later than 60 days after it' (no framework stated). aud-ic-03 stem: 'By when must the auditor communicate...' (no entity type). f5 front: 'Deadline for written communication of SD and MW'. PCAOB AS 1305: the written communication 'should be made prior to the issuance of the auditor's report on the financial statements' (pcaobus.org AS1305, found by web search). aud-communications' aud-cm-22 correctly says 'in a nonissuer audit'.
source: AU-C 265.13; PCAOB AS 1305.04; AS 2201.78-.80 (https://pcaobus.org/oversight/standards/auditing-standards/details/AS1305)
fix: Add a row or line to the Communication section: 'Issuers (AS 1305 / AS 2201): in writing to management and the audit committee before the auditor's report is issued; in an integrated audit, also communicate all deficiencies to management in writing and tell the audit committee.' Change aud-ic-03's stem to 'In an audit of a nonissuer under GAAS, by when...' and f5's front to 'AU-C 265 (nonissuer) deadline...', with a PCAOB contrast on the back.

issue: The 'From deficiency to audit response' table makes the communication-severity label drive the substantive response ('Control deficiency: usually no change to planned substantive work'). In fact the response depends on whether the auditor planned to rely on the deficient control: any deficiency in a control the auditor meant to rely on, with no effective compensating control, raises control risk and requires more substantive work. The SD row's indicator ('reasonably possible misstatement, less than material') is a heuristic, not the standard's definition.
evidence: AU-C 330 / SAS 145: control risk reflects the controls the auditor tests and relies on; if a relied-upon control is deficient, control risk is assessed higher regardless of the AU-C 265 severity label. AU-C 265 defines an SD qualitatively ('less severe than a MW, yet important enough to merit the attention of those charged with governance').
fix: Reframe the table around reliance: 'Was the control relied on? If yes and no effective compensating control: assess control risk higher, then change nature/timing/extent; severity (deficiency/SD/MW) drives communication and, in an integrated audit, the ICFR opinion.' Label the SD indicator as a rule of thumb and quote the definition.

issue: Two defensible answers, and the key contradicts the lesson. The stem's risk is that one person records and deposits receipts, so receipts can be stolen and never recorded or deposited, or lapped. The key, owner review of bank reconciliations, cannot detect this. The lesson's own worked example says 'The bank reconciliation won't catch it — the stolen check was never deposited' and 'A reconciliation ... cannot catch a transaction that never entered either record — that's why lapping ... defeat[s] it.' Distractor (c), mandatory vacation, is listed in the lesson as a compensating control and is the classic way to expose lapping.
evidence: Lesson lines 'When staff are too few to segregate, compensating controls include owner review of bank statements, mandatory vacations, and independent reconciliation' and the worked-example insight quoted above. Key (a) is a reconciliation review, not owner receipt of unopened statements or owner control of incoming receipts (compare aud-ic-05, whose key, 'owner gets the unopened bank statements', is stronger).
source: AU-C 315 application material on small entities (owner-manager oversight); lesson worked example
fix: Make the key clearly best: '(a) The owner opens the mail, lists the receipts, and compares the list with the deposit slips and customer postings.' Alternatively keep (a) but make (c) weaker (e.g., 'Requiring the bookkeeper to sign an annual code-of-conduct acknowledgment'), and explain in (a)'s rationale which part of the scheme owner review catches.

issue: Skill labels are two levels too high. These items are recall or direct application, but they are labeled analysis or evaluation, which inflates the module's higher-order share used in the Blueprint skill-mix targets. aud-ic-17 and aud-ic-18 are also labeled difficulty 3, although they are single-fact recall.
evidence: aud-ic-17 'How does an effective compensating control affect the evaluation of a deficiency?' is a no-scenario rule recall, labeled analysis (should be remembering). aud-ic-18 'Which finding is a strong indicator of a MW?' recalls the AU-C 265 indicator list, with three trivially wrong options; labeled analysis (should be remembering). aud-ic-26: a deviation rate above the tolerable rate means assess control risk higher, a textbook rule; labeled evaluation (should be remembering or application). aud-ic-27: a CEO override is classified as a control-environment deficiency against 'acceptable discretion', 'ITGC failure' and 'irrelevant'; labeled evaluation (should be application). aud-ic-chk2: an immaterial CFO fraud is classified using the indicator list; labeled evaluation (should be application). Practice and exam mix as labeled: R13/A11/An8/E2 of 34. With these and the one-level fixes it becomes R18/A11/An5/E0, i.e. 53% remembering against the 30-40% section band.
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering & Understanding, Application, Analysis, Evaluation); content/sections/aud.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel: aud-ic-17 to remembering, difficulty 1; aud-ic-18 to remembering, difficulty 1-2; aud-ic-26 to application, difficulty 2; aud-ic-27 to application, difficulty 2; aud-ic-chk2 to application. To keep higher-order coverage, add genuine analysis/evaluation items (e.g., aggregate two deficiencies affecting the same account, or judge severity given compensating-control precision and magnitude).

issue: The stem is mis-worded and does not support the key, and the distractors are implausible. 'Approves vendor credit' is a payables/purchasing term; a sales-return credit memo is customer credit. The key ('credit memos that conceal stolen customer payments') needs custody of cash receipts, which the stem never gives the clerk ('handles customer returns' is custody of returned goods). Options (b)-(d) are all unrelated to the clerk's duties, so a difficulty-3 analysis item is answerable by elimination. The key is also the longest option and the only one that repeats 'customer' from the stem.
evidence: Stem: 'A clerk who approves vendor credit also records sales and handles customer returns.' Key explanation: 'Authorization and custody combine with recording', but no cash custody is stated. All three distractors carry the trap irrelevant-fact. cues.md flags 'key longest; key repeats most stem words'.
source: AU-C 315 (segregation of duties); lesson worked example (Pell Hardware)
fix: Rewrite: 'A receivables clerk opens the mail, posts customer payments, and approves credit memos for sales returns. Which misstatement is most likely?' Use plausible same-cycle distractors, e.g. 'Overstated sales from shipments billed twice', 'Understated allowance for doubtful accounts', 'Unrecorded sales returns that overstate inventory'.

issue: Practice MCQ aud-ic-11 and TBS finding 2 use the same scenario (integrated audit, $1.2 million revenue cutoff misstatement, $800,000 materiality, controls missed it, management corrects). Doing either one gives away the TBS rows s2/n2 or the MCQ.

TBS exhibit finding 2: '$1,200,000 of Year 2 shipments recorded as Year 1 revenue ... Management has agreed to correct it'; instructions: 'Overall materiality is $800,000'.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing another)
fix: Change the MCQ to a different account and amounts (e.g., an inventory pricing error of $450,000 against materiality of $300,000), or test a different MW indicator (a restatement of the prior year).

issue: The key 'No, but report those found' overstates the requirement. Only significant deficiencies and material weaknesses must be communicated (in writing). Other deficiencies go to management only if, in the auditor's judgment, they merit management's attention, and they may be communicated orally. The stem's 'search for' is also loose: under SAS 145 the auditor must determine whether deficiencies have been identified from its evaluation of the IC components, but it need not design procedures to find all deficiencies.
evidence: AU-C 265.11-.13: written communication of SD/MW to those charged with governance and management; other deficiencies to management when they are of sufficient importance to merit management's attention. Item explanation: '...communicates significant deficiencies and material weaknesses identified' contradicts the key's 'report those found'.
fix: Stem: 'In a financial statement audit, is the auditor required to design procedures to identify all control deficiencies?' Key: 'No, but it must communicate in writing the significant deficiencies and material weaknesses it identifies.'

issue: The flashcard lists 'a restatement' as a material weakness indicator. The indicator is a restatement of previously issued financial statements to correct a material misstatement. A revision for an immaterial error is not an indicator. The lesson states it correctly.
evidence: f6 back: 'Senior management fraud (any amount), a restatement, an auditor-detected material misstatement, ineffective oversight by TCWG.' Lesson: 'a restatement to correct a material misstatement'.
source: AU-C 265.A11; PCAOB AS 2201.69
fix: Change to 'a restatement of previously issued FS to correct a material misstatement'.

issue: The flashcard back defines a possibility, not a deficiency: it omits 'a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control such that...'. The combination element is often tested.
evidence: f3 back: 'A reasonable possibility that a material misstatement won't be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis.' The glossary entry has the full definition.
fix: Back: 'A deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis.'

issue: The docreview can be solved with no knowledge. All four highlighted phrases are wrong as drafted, and three of the four cells offer only two options (the original and the answer), so always changing the original scores 100%. In p1 the third option ('the company's bank') is not plausible.
evidence: p1 options: Controller / Board / bank, original wrong. p2, p3, p4 options: [original, answer], originals all wrong (originals wrong: 4 of 4).

Give every cell 3-4 options with plausible errors, e.g. p1 'Management only' / 'Management and the Board of Directors' / 'the Controller'; p4 'before the report release date only' / 'within 30 days...' / 'no later than 60 days after the report release date'. Add cells for the required MW/SD definitions (AU-C 265.14(a)).

issue: The p4 explanation misstates the rule: 'AU-C 265 requires the written communication by the documentation completion date (60 days).' AU-C 265 requires it no later than 60 days after the report release date, and best by the report release date. The documentation completion date is a separate AU-C 230 concept: the date the final file is assembled, which can be earlier than day 60.
evidence: The explanation text is quoted above; the lesson and flashcard f5 state 'best by the report release date, and no later than 60 days after it'.
source: AU-C 265.13 and application material; AU-C 230 (documentation completion date)
fix: Explanation: 'AU-C 265: communicate in writing on a timely basis, best by the report release date and no later than 60 days after it.'

issue: The suggested minutes (and the r3 skill label) are generous for the work involved.
evidence: aud-tbs-r3-265-letter: 15 min and 'analysis' for 4 cells, 3 of them binary choices (about 5 min, application). aud-tbs-x2-controls: 25 min for 10 dropdown rows, 7 of them binary (about 12-15 min). The real AUD exam allows about 17 min per TBS for much denser tasks.

issue: A cross-part answer cue in an exam-pool TBS (used in aud-mock-1). The 'asr' part asks 'Which assertion does each effective control primarily address?' and lists only items 1, 2 and 5. This reveals that e1, e2 and e5 are 'Effective control' and, by elimination, that e3, e4 and e6 are 'Deficiency'. The whole eval part (6 of 10 scored rows) is given away.

source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing another), applied to TBS parts
fix: Make asr cover all six items with an extra option 'Not applicable — deficient control', or reword the prompt to 'For items 1, 2 and 5, which assertion does the control address?' and add asr rows for some deficient items (e.g., item 6 relates to accuracy of revenue).

issue: The d2 explanation calls the three-way match an automated control ('automated controls such as the three-way match can't be relied on'), but the exhibit describes a manual match ('Accounts payable matches the PO, receiving report, and vendor invoice'). The ITGC lesson the explanation tries to teach (program-change failures undermine automated controls) is therefore illustrated with an example the exhibit contradicts.
evidence: Exhibit item 3 vs part def/d2 explanation.
source: aud-it-controls lesson (ITGCs support reliance on automated controls)
fix: Make exhibit item 3 'The system performs a three-way match and blocks unmatched invoices from payment', or change the d2 explanation to cite an automated control actually in the exhibit.

issue: Finding 1 and the s1 explanation decide SD vs control deficiency on a 'more than inconsequential' magnitude threshold. That test comes from superseded PCAOB AS No. 2 (2004) and was removed by AS No. 5 (now AS 2201) in 2007. The current SD definition is qualitative: less severe than a MW, yet important enough to merit the attention of those responsible for oversight. Students learn an obsolete bright-line test.
evidence: Exhibit: 'The potential misstatement is estimated to be well below materiality but more than inconsequential.' s1 explanation: '...reasonably possible and more than inconsequential but less than material, and important enough to merit the audit committee's attention.' AS 2201 Appendix A defines SD without any 'inconsequential' threshold (review/reference/aud-standards.md §4).
source: PCAOB AS 2201 Appendix A (A11 significant deficiency); AS 2201.62-.70
fix: Rewrite the exhibit fact as a judgment cue under AS 2201, e.g. 'The deviations affect a significant account; the potential misstatement is below materiality, but the deficiency is important enough to merit the audit committee's attention.' Drop 'more than inconsequential' from the s1 explanation.

issue: Distractor (a) 'No effect, because the auditor corrected it' implies the auditor corrects the client's financial statements. Management records corrections, and the auditor proposes them.
evidence: aud-ic-09 option (a) text.
source: AU-C 450 (auditor requests management to correct misstatements)
fix: 'No effect, because management corrected it after the auditor proposed an adjustment.'

issue: The lesson uses only COSO component names. Since SAS 145, AU-C 315 names them 'the entity's risk assessment process', 'the entity's process to monitor the system of internal control' and 'the information system and communication', and exam items written from AU-C 315 use those names. The lesson also cites AU-C 315 as '(Understanding internal control)' without noting the SAS 145 revision.
evidence: Lesson component table and citations; SAS 145 effective for periods ending on or after Dec 15, 2023 (review/reference/aud-standards.md §2).
source: AU-C 315 as amended by SAS 145
fix: Add a column 'AU-C 315 (SAS 145) name' to the component table, and cite 'AU-C 315 (as amended by SAS 145)'.
